# Service Menu Build — Execution Plan for Grace

• **Split into two documents NOW, not one:** Coaches need pricing/commission structure + service boundaries (e.g., "nutrition advice stops here, refer to nutritionist"). Members get clean pricing + what's included per tier. Different audiences, different problems. Start with member-facing — that drives revenue.

• **Audit what you're *actually* selling first:** Before writing menus, spend 2 hours shadowing coaches and recording every service variation happening (1-on-1 rates, class bundles, nutrition consultations, challenges, PT packages). You probably have 6+ undocumented offerings. Write what exists, then clean it up.

• **Price against Belfast market + perceived value, not costs:** Find 3 comparable women's gyms (Dublin, Manchester, online). Price your premium offerings (small group PT, nutrition coaching) 10-15% above them — positioning The Forge as specialist, not commodity. Add a "why we cost this" line for coaches to reference.

• **Build a simple visual one-pager for the gym floor:** Not a 10-page brochure. A4 laminated sheet showing tier options (Basic Membership → Personal Training Add-on → Nutrition Package) with price and 3-bullet benefits per tier. Coaches use this to upsell naturally in conversations.

• **Test pricing with 5 loyal members this week:** Show them the draft menu, ask "does this feel right?" One conversation beats endless internal debating. You'll catch if someone expects something not listed.

**Timeline: Draft by end of this week, test + refine next week, launch week after.**

## REVENUE — FIX CHURN & UNLOCK PRICING

• **Churn spike May 2026 (12.7%) is killing momentum.** You grew members 111→135 (Jan–Jun) but lost 17 in May alone. Post-relocation wobble? Survey those 17 leavers this week. May churn erased ~£1,600 of potential recurring revenue. Implement exit interviews + win-back campaign (discounted return offer) immediately — this is your single biggest leak.

• **Revenue per member dropped to £118–119 (May–Jun) from £130–138 (Feb–Apr).** You're either discounting to fill the new studio or members aren't using add-on classes/PT. Audit your pricing: benchmark against competitors, and if you're underpriced, raise membership fees 5–8% (£8–12/month) starting next billing cycle. Test a premium tier (unlimited + priority booking) at +15%.

• **Fill quiet off-peak slots with low-friction upsells.** Early morning (6–7am) and midweek (Tue/Wed 10am–3pm) classes typically run 30–40% capacity in gyms your size. Bundle off-peak class packs (10 sessions £35) for members, or sell to non-members as trial entry. Target £200–300/month new revenue with zero fixed cost.

---

• **June cash out (£20,644) vs May (£16,639) jumped +24% despite flat revenue.** New studio costs settling? Break down June spend by category (rent, payroll, utilities, stock). If staffing grew post-relocation, model your fixed payroll as % of revenue: should sit 35–40% for a gym. If it's 45%+, you're overstaffed — shift to part-time/zero-hours for quiet hours.

• **Supplier costs: request invoices for last 3 months.** Flag any monthly subscriptions (software, insurance, cleaning, supplies) running >5% of revenue (currently £750+). Renegotiate annual vs monthly contracts with your cleaning/maintenance provider — aim for 10–15% saving by bundling or switching to on-demand.
